options.name: Input-drift metric monitoring
options.description: Uses quantitative comparisons of production inputs with a reference distribution to detect input-distribution change. It focuses on drift metrics without requiring broader behavioral or availability evidence.

options.name: Policy-entropy monitoring
options.description: Uses policy entropy as the primary evidence of changes in exploration, action uncertainty, or behavioral stability after deployment.

options.name: Environment-and-domain drift diagnosis
options.description: Combines technical or business drift assessment with diagnosis of changed environment dynamics, rather than treating degradation as model failure alone.

options.name: Comprehensive multi-signal drift monitoring
options.description: Correlates input drift, feature availability, policy entropy, technical or business signals, and environment-change evidence to diagnose complex production degradation.

options.name: Input-and-behavior monitoring with availability checks
options.description: Combines input-distribution evidence and policy-behavior evidence with technical or business signals and checks that required inference features remain available.

options.name: Input monitoring with feature-availability checks
options.description: Detects both changes in the input distribution and missing or broken inference features, treating telemetry completeness as part of drift detection.

options.name: Output-quality metrics and feedback
options.description: Accuracy, perplexity, user feedback, false-negative rates, and related signals assess whether outputs remain useful and safe.

options.name: Combined drift and quality monitoring
options.description: Joint monitoring of input drift and output quality provides broader coverage than either evidence source alone.

options.name: Proxy objective metrics
options.description: Measurable proxy metrics stand in for complex objectives while requiring checks for divergence from the true goal.

options.name: Evaluator consistency diagnostics
options.description: Metrics such as conflict rate detect inconsistent or position-sensitive automated evaluation.

options.name: Novel-situation and capability monitoring
options.description: Monitor novelty and estimated agent capability to identify situations the deployed agent may not handle.

options.name: Real-time regret analysis
options.description: Using live regret estimates to measure deviation from desirable or optimal behavior.

options.name: Statistical performance-degradation testing
options.description: Apply statistical tests to detect changes in episodic reward or production performance.

options.name: Multi-metric quality monitoring
options.description: Using complementary metrics rather than a single optimized metric to evaluate deployed-agent quality.

options.name: Cross-metric regression monitoring
options.description: Detecting cases where an optimized metric improves while related quality metrics deteriorate.

options.name: Explainable decision auditing
options.description: Explainability mechanisms provide auditable evidence about the basis of AI decisions.

options.name: Ongoing bias monitoring
options.description: Continuously monitor bias and annotator-subjectivity effects in deployed behavior and feedback.

options.name: Automated threshold alerting
options.description: Monitoring infrastructure raises alerts when drift or quality metrics cross configured thresholds.

options.name: Unhandled-situation alarm escalation
options.description: Raise operational alarms when the agent encounters hazardous or unhandled situations.

options.name: Adversarial red-team probing
options.description: AI or human red teams actively search deployed policies and reward models for exploitable strategies.

options.name: Anomaly and divergence detection
options.description: Anomaly detection, KL divergence, and related statistical methods identify unusual behavior or policy deviation.

options.name: Behavioral inspection and plausibility checking
options.description: Monitoring inspects actual actions and checks whether behavior is plausible rather than trusting reward scores alone.

options.name: Environment-variation robustness testing
options.description: Monitoring varies deployment conditions slightly to reveal brittle or exploitative policies.

options.name: Shortcut and spurious-correlation probing
options.description: Detection probes whether agents rely on shortcuts or spurious features instead of intended task-relevant behavior.

options.name: Process-level supervision
options.description: Supervise intermediate reasoning and actions rather than relying only on final outcomes to detect reward exploitation.

options.name: Chain-of-thought monitoring
options.description: Inspecting model reasoning traces to detect reward hacking and supervise deployed behavior.

options.name: Strong chain-of-thought supervision
options.description: Applying strong optimization or supervision pressure directly to reasoning traces.

options.name: Victim fine-tuning as insufficient adversarial defense
options.description: Fine-tuning against known adversarial policies fails to prevent vulnerability to newly generated attacks.

options.name: Diverse reward-hack training tests
options.description: Behavioral testing exposes agents to easy, hard, and concealed reward-hacking cases to assess mitigation generalization.

options.name: Dual-capability evaluator design
options.description: Behavioral probing uses evaluators with different capabilities to expose both obvious and concealed reward hacks.

options.name: Inoculation prompting
options.description: Behavioral probing prompts agents to recognize or resist reward-hacking opportunities during evaluation and training.

options.name: Mild grading-script-pass prompt
options.description: Behavioral probing uses a mild prompt that frames success as passing the grading script.

options.name: Controlled feature-perturbation probing
options.description: Rewrite or perturb suspected spoiler features to test behavioral and reward sensitivity.

options.name: Hidden-hint faithfulness probing
options.description: Inject neutral or adversarial hints and compare decisions with disclosed reasoning to test faithfulness.

options.name: Reasoning-propensity measurement
options.description: Measuring how readily an agent produces or relies on particular reasoning patterns to assess monitoring effectiveness.

options.name: Single behavioral-model monitoring
options.description: Use one separate language model to inspect agent reasoning, actions, or outputs for reward hacking and misbehavior.

options.name: Targeted reward-discrepancy monitoring
options.description: Combine behavioral-model review with outcome and feature-level checks for cases where measured reward diverges from task success or reflects unintended features.

options.name: Behavioral-trajectory monitoring
options.description: Combine behavioral-model review with action-sequence analysis to identify anomalous or objective-misaligned trajectories.

options.name: Training-integrated behavioral monitoring
options.description: Run behavioral-model checks and anomaly rules within the training or policy-update loop so degradation can be detected during optimization.

options.name: Training-integrated outcome monitoring
options.description: Detect reward-behavior discrepancies through anomaly checks embedded in the training loop, supporting automated intervention when performance deteriorates.

options.name: Integrated reward-integrity ensemble
options.description: Use a coordinated set of behavioral, outcome, reward-path, trajectory, statistical, and feature-influence signals to detect manipulation and reward hacking from multiple perspectives.

options.name: Comprehensive reward-hacking monitoring stack
options.description: Combine broad automated detection with training-loop checks, human-preference disagreement, and internal interpretability signals to monitor both observable behavior and the mechanisms producing reward.

options.name: Process filtering
options.description: Monitoring evaluates the agent’s intermediate process rather than trusting only final rewards or outcomes.

options.name: Thorough reward-hacking testing
options.description: Deep testing is treated as an adopted validation practice, despite competitive pressure that may encourage shortcuts.

options.name: Holdout-environment reward-tampering testing
options.description: Reward-tampering likelihood is measured in environments withheld from training to test behavioral generalization.

options.name: Reasoning-penalization filtering
options.description: Penalize reasoning judged problematic as a filtering or mitigation mechanism.

options.name: Verifier cascade filtering
options.description: Cascade precise rule-based checks with adaptive model-based verification to filter reward-hacking behavior.

options.name: Rubric-decomposed reward filtering
options.description: Use interpretable multidimensional rubric criteria to construct and audit reward signals.

options.name: Veto-based reward aggregation
options.description: Let critical defense or veto criteria invalidate an otherwise high aggregate reward.

options.name: Gated intermediate-reward accumulation
options.description: Accumulate intermediate verification rewards only after long-term outcome thresholds are met.

options.name: Reward-hacking verbalization training
options.description: Train agents to acknowledge shortcut exploitation in reasoning traces for improved detectability.

options.name: Unhackable reward-function guarantee
options.description: The design attempts to guarantee that reward functions cannot be exploited.

options.name: Reward-code debugging as primary remedy
options.description: Reward hacking is treated as an implementation bug to fix through reward-code debugging.

options.name: Single-metric optimization
options.description: The system optimizes one metric without complementary measures.

options.name: Reward-logic unit testing
options.description: Testing reward implementation logic before deployment to expose misspecification and gaming vulnerabilities.

options.name: Reward-hack-resistant training objective
options.description: Filtering and training use objectives designed to resist exploitation beyond simple outcome-based rewards.

options.name: Outcome-based reward objective
options.description: Filtering and training use a simple outcome score as the baseline reward objective.

options.name: Human-led feedback with selective AI augmentation
options.description: Human evaluators remain the primary source of post-deployment feedback, with AI-assisted evaluation added when it can improve coverage or reduce annotation effort.

options.name: Comprehensive human-and-AI feedback
options.description: Post-deployment evaluation combines human judgments, independent AI evaluation, and hybrid human-and-AI feedback channels to maximize coverage and scalability.

options.name: Privacy-preserving aggregate usage feedback
options.description: Population-level usage signals guide improvement without exposing individual users’ operational data.

options.name: Structured human annotation
options.description: Human-led, structured correction and annotation provide reliable feedback for ambiguous or complex outputs.

options.name: Periodic model retraining
options.description: Scheduled retraining or model refreshes incorporate accumulated production changes at discrete intervals.

options.name: Fine-tuning and domain adaptation
options.description: New or domain-specific data updates an existing model without rebuilding the full system.

options.name: Online continual learning
options.description: Streaming production data and feedback drive ongoing model updates for applications requiring high adaptivity.

options.name: Retrieval-based mitigation
options.description: Updated external context temporarily addresses knowledge or drift problems without immediately changing model parameters.

options.name: Prompt-template adjustment
options.description: Prompt or instruction changes remediate detected behavior without requiring a full model update.

options.name: User-specific adaptation
options.description: Feedback and usage data personalize updates to an individual user, developer, or project context.

options.name: Frequent parameter-efficient updates
options.description: PEFT methods such as LoRA enable smaller and more frequent model changes.

options.name: Continual pre-training
options.description: Refresh the model periodically or continuously with recent or domain-specific data before deployment updates.

options.name: Localized model editing
options.description: Applying targeted parameter edits for a small number of changed facts or behaviors.

options.name: Original-data rehearsal for capability retention
options.description: Mix historical training data into update data to retain prior capabilities during adaptation.

options.name: Historical-sample rehearsal cache
options.description: Retain important historical samples and replay them during post-deployment updates.

options.name: Post-recovery learning-rate reduction
options.description: Training resumes after recovery with a reduced learning rate to dampen oscillation.

options.name: Training-loop-integrated monitoring
options.description: Monitoring hooks are embedded in training or rollout execution to observe performance continuously.

options.name: Preference and reward-model training
options.description: Training uses human preference comparisons to fit a reward model that guides policy optimization.

options.name: PPO and GRPO policy optimization
options.description: Policy parameters are optimized with PPO or GRPO after reward or preference modeling.

options.name: Distributed actor-critic training
options.description: Training distributes actor-critic learning across multiple workers for scalable policy improvement.

options.name: Asynchronous policy training
options.description: Policy updates proceed asynchronously to support continuous improvement without blocking production interaction.

options.name: Federated RL training
options.description: RL training is distributed across environments or user populations while preserving privacy and reducing communication.

options.name: Reward shaping
options.description: Training modifies reward structure to guide behavior toward desired objectives.

options.name: Conservative offline RL training
options.description: Train policy updates conservatively from historical production logs without disrupting live operation.

options.name: Co-evolving policy-reward training
options.description: Adapting the reward mechanism alongside policy updates rather than treating reward as static.

options.name: Light reasoning-trace optimization
options.description: Applying limited optimization pressure to reasoning traces as a cautious policy-training approach.

options.name: Expert-led review
options.description: Post-deployment monitoring review and intervention are performed primarily by human experts who inspect sampled or problematic behavior and provide safety judgments or corrections.

options.name: Cross-functional operational oversight
options.description: Human experts and multiple organizational teams jointly review evidence, handle alerts, maintain the deployed agent, and approve changes.

options.name: Human-gated scalable oversight
options.description: Human oversight remains the primary safeguard while review and intervention mechanisms are designed to remain effective as agent capability and deployment demand increase.

options.name: Cross-functional scalable oversight
options.description: Cross-team maintenance and intervention workflows are combined with oversight mechanisms designed to scale across deployment volume and monitoring demand.

options.name: Reward-penalty safety mechanism
options.description: Safety costs are folded into the task reward through weighted penalties compatible with standard RL pipelines.

options.name: Constrained policy optimization
options.description: Safety constraints are incorporated directly into policy learning rather than applied only after training.

options.name: Conservative policy updates
options.description: Policy changes are limited relative to proven baseline behavior to reduce catastrophic degradation.

options.name: Hybrid policy with fallback behavior
options.description: Supervised components provide safety constraints, initialization, or fallback behavior when RL policies perform poorly.

options.name: Open-world deployment design
options.description: Agents are designed to recognize and handle observations that differ from training conditions.

options.name: Closed-world deployment assumption
options.description: Explicitly rejected assumption that deployment conditions match the training environment.

options.name: Classical primal-dual safety enforcement
options.description: Use classical primal-dual or Lagrangian mechanisms as the safety enforcement approach.

options.name: Observed-state-only safety constraints
options.description: Define safety constraints solely over measurable state variables.

options.name: Ethical and fairness governance
options.description: Ethical frameworks and fairness controls constrain reward-model development and deployed agent behavior.

options.name: Regulatory accountability controls
options.description: Accountability, transparency, and compliance controls govern acceptable production AI behavior.

options.name: Deployment-distribution safety assessment
options.description: Evaluate whether agent behavior remains safe under the distribution encountered after deployment.

options.name: Training-compliance-only safety assurance
options.description: Treat compliance during training as sufficient evidence of deployed-agent safety.

options.name: Prompt-injection defense
options.description: Real-time controls block adversarial prompts intended to manipulate the agent into unsafe outputs.

options.name: Restricted-topic response filtering
options.description: Policy filters forbid responses on sensitive or off-policy topics.

options.name: Layered safety enforcement
options.description: Safety combines policy, uncertainty, stress testing, OOD monitoring, shielding, and safe action gating rather than one mechanism.

options.name: Safety-rule violation logging
options.description: Instrumenting runtime safety rules and counting actions that breach them.

options.name: Runtime adaptive shielding
options.description: A runtime shield adapts action intervention when monitoring detects uncertainty or distributional shift.

options.name: Business-rule validation
options.description: Generated or extracted outputs are checked against structured domain and business rules.

options.name: Importance-sampling evaluation
options.description: Off-policy estimates correct for differences between logged behavior and the evaluated policy, but may have high variance.

options.name: Fitted Q-evaluation
options.description: Value estimation through fitted action-value functions offers an alternative with potentially lower variance and approximation requirements.

options.name: Offline policy evaluation
options.description: Logged production experience is used to estimate policy value and safety before or during deployment.

options.name: Automated evaluation metrics
options.description: Fast automatic metrics assess output quality and improvement during policy evaluation.

options.name: Domain-specific evaluation benchmarks
options.description: Industry or task-specific benchmarks assess correctness against the deployed agent's domain requirements.

options.name: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation
options.description: A stronger language model compares outputs or assesses reasoning quality as an automated evaluator.

options.name: Validation-gated deployment
options.description: A changed policy is deployed only after validation checks pass.

options.name: Shadow policy evaluation
options.description: Candidate policies make observer-only decisions or run on a traffic subset before live action.

options.name: Dataset validation and schema checking
options.description: Policy evaluation and retraining pipelines validate data integrity and schemas before use.

options.name: Coverage-aware sampling and augmentation
options.description: Evaluation data are stratified and augmented to represent rare, production-relevant cases.

options.name: On-policy evaluation unavailable offline
options.description: Evaluation requiring fresh environment interaction is not used when deployment decisions must rely solely on logged experience.

options.name: Effective sample size diagnostic
options.description: Offline evaluation uses effective sample size as supporting evidence for importance-weight reliability.

options.name: Effective sample size as primary evidence
options.description: Offline evaluation treats effective sample size as the primary reliability signal.

options.name: Canary policy validation
options.description: Expose a candidate policy to limited live traffic before broader deployment.

options.name: Production A/B policy testing
options.description: Comparing a changed policy with the incumbent policy on live production traffic.

options.name: Trajectory-focused telemetry
options.description: Production telemetry retains complete state-action-reward trajectories as the primary behavioral record for analysis and offline learning, without requiring broad capture of intermediate actions or final outputs.

options.name: Multi-stage behavioral telemetry
options.description: Production telemetry spans multiple points in the agent’s behavior, combining trajectory records with intermediate actions, final outputs, and operational outcome codes to support end-to-end monitoring and evaluation.

options.name: Unvalidated contextual telemetry
options.description: Telemetry retains contextual metadata about the action, such as the behavior policy that generated it or the agent’s natural-language reasoning, without requiring empirical validation of the reasoning trace.

options.name: Validated reasoning telemetry
options.description: Telemetry retains natural-language reasoning traces and subjects them to empirical checks of whether they faithfully reflect the agent’s behavior before using them for oversight.

options.name: Registry-based rollback
options.description: Restore a deployed agent by automatically switching to a known-good registered version when monitoring detects degraded behavior. This option centers recovery on deployment-version reversal rather than on restoring runtime state or healing the agent in place.

options.name: Integrated stateful self-healing recovery
options.description: Recover the agent through a coordinated mechanism that combines persistent checkpoints, automatic healing, registry-based rollback, and restoration of stateful model state. This option supports recovery when simply changing the deployed version is insufficient because the agent's runtime or learned state is also compromised.

options.name: Rollback verification and audit
options.description: Exercise rollback regularly and retain trigger, version, notification, and recovery records.

options.name: Automated rollback drills
options.description: Recovery procedures are exercised regularly to verify that rollback remains operational.

options.name: Tail-latency-observed serving
options.description: Inference runs with explicit monitoring of high-percentile serving latency as the primary operational capacity signal. This option emphasizes detecting serving degradation rather than specifying a broader serving topology.

options.name: Full platform-integrated scalable serving
options.description: Inference is deployed as stateless, horizontally scalable services with redundant critical components, separated training and inference environments, gateway-based routing, and rate limiting. This is a comprehensive platform architecture for managing production capacity and availability.

options.name: Isolated latency-controlled serving
options.description: Inference uses stateless services with Kubernetes scaling and rate limiting, while training is isolated from production inference and tail latency is monitored. This option prioritizes production stability and controlled capacity without the full gateway-and-redundancy stack.

options.name: Least-privilege role-based access control
options.description: Operational permissions are separated by role and limited to required capabilities.

options.name: Secrets-managed operational credentials
options.description: Credentials and API keys are protected through dedicated secrets management.

options.name: Authenticated inference access
options.description: Require caller authentication and authorization before accepting inference requests.

options.name: Prometheus-Grafana monitoring stack
options.description: Infrastructure and ML monitoring are implemented with a dedicated metrics and dashboard stack.

options.name: Workflow-orchestrated monitoring integration
options.description: Monitoring connects to CI/CD or workflow systems through automated orchestration and service interfaces.

options.name: Tool-mediated agent execution
options.description: Agent actions are evaluated through an operational tool interface that mediates codebase or environment changes.

options.name: Interaction audit logging
options.description: Every interaction is retained for traceability, explainability, regulatory review, and compliance oversight.

options.name: Reproducible monitoring infrastructure
options.description: Publishing reference implementations and experiment artifacts to enable independent monitoring validation and extension.
